title: Sell Mineral Rights in Overly, ND
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Overly, ND
metaDescription: Hold mineral rights near Overly, ND in Bottineau County? We buy flank-area interests directly and can explain what yours is realistically worth.
heroLead: Overly is one of the smallest towns we cover, and most of the mineral interests tied to it have sat untouched in a family filing cabinet for two generations or more.
intro: There isn't much drilling activity around Overly today, and there hasn't been much in recent memory, but Bottineau County land was leased widely at different points over the last century, and plenty of families here still hold the mineral rights that came with an old homestead even after the surface was sold off or the farm passed to someone outside the family.

sections.heading: Undeveloped doesn't mean worthless
paragraphs: A mineral interest with no current well on it can still have value, either because it sits near acreage that has seen activity, or because a buyer is willing to hold it for the long term at a modest price. We check recent leasing and permitting activity near your specific tract before telling you what we think it's worth, rather than assuming nothing is happening just because your last statement was years ago.

sections.heading: Clearing up ownership before anything else
paragraphs: Because so much of the mineral ownership around Overly traces back to early homestead patents, it's common for a single tract to be split among a dozen or more distant cousins by now, most of whom have no idea the others exist. If that sounds like your situation, we can research the full ownership picture and, if you'd like, help coordinate with other family members on the same tract.

sections.heading: Why we still check even quiet ground carefully
paragraphs: We've had Overly-area owners assume nothing was worth pursuing, only to find a small but real lease payment or nearby permit they didn't know about. Bottineau County's activity is modest compared to the Bakken core, but modest isn't the same as nothing, and it's worth a proper look before you decide either way.

faqs.question: There's no well anywhere near our Overly property. Should we still bother?
faqs.answer: It's worth a quick check. Even undeveloped mineral interests sometimes have buyers, and it costs you nothing to find out what your specific tract might be worth.

faqs.question: We think other relatives might also own a share of this interest. What then?
faqs.answer: That's common with old homestead-era mineral rights. We can research the full ownership chain and work with you and other co-owners together if that's easier than everyone handling it separately.

faqs.question: Do you charge anything to look into our Overly mineral rights?
faqs.answer: No. We research title and current activity at no cost before we ever make an offer, so you can decide with real information rather than guesswork.

faqs.question: How long has your family been buying North Dakota minerals like this?
faqs.answer: We sold our own family's minerals through this same process before we ever started buying, which is part of why we walk owners through it as carefully as we do.
